To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Askaryan emission from a particle shower in a dielectric is independent of the shower depth below the surface, and (2) a recent limit on the neutrinos flux above 10{exp}22{exp}eV, obtained by the NuMoon project with the Westerbok Radio Telescope, can also be interpreted as a limit on the ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray flux.
the radio emission from particle showers below the surface of a dielectric is independent of the shower depth, and that this can be used to set limits on the flux of cosmic rays.
the Askaryan pulse transmitted through a dielectric surface is independent of depth and that the limit on the neutrinos from NuMoon can be used to constrain the cosmic rays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of ultra-high-energy particles, such as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray nuclei, neutrinos and photons, which interact with matter and produce secondary particles.
the study of the propagation of electromagnetic waves in the atmosphere and in particular the interaction of electromagnetic waves with the atmosphere and with cosmic ray showers.
the physics of ultra-high-energy particles and their interaction with matter.

the Askaryan emission from particle showers in a medium just beneath the surface can be detected from very far away, which opens up the possibility to use this effect to detect particle showers in the Earth's crust.
